mainTopic: The amount of wine one must carry on שבת to be liable (diluted-cup measure), the כזית measure for dried wine and אביי's rejection of רב יוסף's comparison, and the spelling of 'גמיאה' for milk.
overview: On the previous amud, רבא ruled that one who carries undiluted wine on שבת is liable for an amount that, once diluted with water, makes a רביעית. The גמרא supports this from the משנה and a ברייתא, and shows it fits רבא's rule that real wine takes three parts water. אביי raises two objections: a משנה describes diluted wine as only 2:1, and water left in the jug should not count. רבא answers that the 2:1 mix is for weak Sharon wine or only for color, and that the small amount of strong wine counts because it is significant on its own. Next, a תוספתא teaches in the name of רבי נתן that dried-up wine is measured by a כזית. רב יוסף claims that רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה holds the same idea, since he says a רביעית of blood congeals into a כזית. אביי rejects this comparison, because thin wine and thick blood shrink differently when they dry. Finally, the גמרא asks whether the משנה's word for a gulp of milk is spelled with an א or an ע. רב נחמן בר יצחק proves from a פסוק that it is spelled with an א, and the גמרא opens another spelling question that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Support for רבא from the משנה and ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רבא's measure for carrying wine was already taught: the משנה says 'enough to dilute a cup', a ברייתא adds 'a nice cup', and the סיפא says other liquids need a רביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: We already learned this: One who carries out wine is liable for enough to dilute a cup. And a ברייתא taught on it: enough to dilute a nice cup. And the end of the משנה teaches: 'And all other liquids are measured by a רביעית.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings proof that רבא's ruling is already found in the משנה. It does this by putting together three pieces of text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A 'nice cup' is a full, proper cup of drink. The סיפא tells us that the proper amount for drinks is a רביעית. So the wine needed is just enough to make a רביעית of diluted drink, which is exactly רבא's measure.

keyTerms.meaning: We already learned it (in a משנה)
Diluting a cup (mixing wine with water)
The latter clause of a משנה
A quarter of a לוג, the standard measure for drinks

steps.confusionAlert: The wine itself is not a רביעית. The diluted drink is a רביעית. Since strong wine is mixed with a lot of water, the actual wine carried is much smaller.

phrases.english: We already learned: One who carries out wine —
is liable for enough to dilute a cup,
and a Baraita taught regarding it:
enough to dilute a nice (proper) cup.
And the latter clause teaches:
"And all other liquids — with a quarter-log."
phrases.notes: This shows that a proper drink is a רביעית.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's ruling from the end of the previous daf.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's ruling that the measure for wine is enough to make a diluted רביעית
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה ('כדי מזיגת כוס'), the ברייתא ('כוס יפה'), and the סיפא ('שאר כל המשקין ברביעית')

steps.title: רבא follows his own rule: real wine takes three parts water
steps.stepSummary: רבא is consistent with his other ruling: wine that cannot take three parts water to one part wine is not real wine. That is why a quarter of a רביעית of wine makes a full diluted רביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא follows his own reasoning, for רבא said: Any wine that cannot carry three parts water on one part wine is not wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains where the math in רבא's ruling comes from, using another ruling of רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If real wine is one part wine to three parts water, then the wine is one quarter of the cup. So a quarter of a רביעית of wine plus water makes a full רביעית. This sets up the numbers that אביי will attack next.

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own reasoning (consistent with his other view)
Carries / can hold (can take on water)

phrases.english: And Rava follows his own reasoning,
for Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל חַמְרָא דְּלָא דָּרֵי עַל חַד תְּלָת מַיָּא
phrases.english: Any wine that cannot carry three parts water on one part
is not wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the 1:3 ratio behind the measure that step 1 supported.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Real wine must be able to take three parts water to one part wine.

steps.title: אביי's first objection: the Sharon wine mix is 2:1
steps.stepSummary: אביי says he has two objections. The first: a משנה describes diluted wine as two parts water and one part wine, not three to one.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: There are two objections to this. One, as we learned in a משנה: And 'the diluted' means two parts water and one part wine, from Sharon wine.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבא's 1:3 ratio using a משנה about diluted wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה (in נדה, used to identify a shade of red blood) describes 'diluted wine' as 2:1 water to wine. If normal dilution is 2:1, then wine is a third of the cup, not a quarter. That would make רבא's measure wrong.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
There are two refutations of the matter —
One, as we learned in a Mishnah:

phrases.aramaic: וְהַמָּזוּג שְׁנֵי חֶלְקֵי מַיִם וְאֶחָד יַיִן,
phrases.english: And 'the diluted' is two parts water and one part wine,
from the Sharon wine.
phrases.notes: This משנה is about the colors of blood in נדה.

steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that wine is diluted one part to three parts water
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה gives the dilution as 1:2, which would make the wine a third of the cup, not a quarter.

steps.title: אביי's second objection: the water is still in the jug
steps.stepSummary: אביי's second objection: how can water that is not being carried (it is still in the jug at home) count toward the amount of wine he carried?
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore: the water is in the jug, and it joins together?!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a second objection, this one based on logic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By רבא's measure, the person carries only a tiny amount of wine, a quarter of a רביעית. The water that would turn it into a real drink is not with him at all. אביי asks how missing water can make the tiny amount count as significant.

keyTerms.meaning: Join together / combine toward a measure

phrases.english: And furthermore:
The water is in the jug, and they combine?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second of אביי's two announced objections.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's measure of a quarter רביעית of undiluted wine
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Water that is not carried should not help reach the liability amount. The wine actually carried is too small to drink as it is.

steps.title: רבא: Sharon wine is unusually weak
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers the first objection: Sharon wine is different because it is weak, so it can only take two parts water.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: What you said, two parts water and one part wine from Sharon wine — Sharon wine is different, because it is weak.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers אביי's first objection by saying that the משנה is talking about a special, weak wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normal strong wine takes three parts water. Sharon wine is weaker, so the משנה used only two parts water. The משנה is an exception and does not prove anything about regular wine.

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
That which you said,
two parts water and one part wine
from the Sharon wine —
Sharon wine is different, because it is weak.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the source to a special case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's 2:1 mix is the normal way to dilute wine.
steps.terutzMaskana: 2:1 applies only to weak Sharon wine. Normal wine still takes 1:3.

steps.title: רבא's second answer: color versus taste
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives another answer: the משנה's mix is about how the wine looks, its color. For taste, wine needs more water.
steps.simpleTranslation: Alternatively, there it is for appearance, but for taste it needs more.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a second, different answer to אביי's first objection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in נדה is trying to describe a color. For a color sample, 2:1 is enough. But to make a properly tasting drink, which is what matters for carrying, you need more water. So the 1:3 ratio stands.

phrases.english: Alternatively, there it is because of appearance,
but for taste it needs more (water).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the same objection as step 5.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 2:1 mix describes a normal drink.
steps.terutzMaskana: The 2:1 mix is only for matching a color. A drink needs more water.

steps.title: רבא: on שבת we need something significant, and this is
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers the second objection: the water is not actually being combined. For שבת we only need the carried item to be significant, and this small amount of strong wine is significant because it can make a full drink.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what you said, 'the water is in the jug and they combine?!' — regarding שבת we need something significant, and this too is significant.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers אביי's second objection by explaining the reason behind the measure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule for carrying on שבת is that the item must be worth something. We are not adding the water to the wine. Instead, a small amount of strong wine is valuable because it can be turned into a proper cup. So it counts as significant by itself.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא's measure stands: a quarter רביעית of strong wine counts, because it is valuable enough to make a full diluted רביעית. The 2:1 משנה is either about weak Sharon wine or only about color.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a basic rule of שבת measures: liability depends on whether the carried object is significant to people, not on technical volume alone.

phrases.english: And what you said:
'The water is in the jug and they combine' —
regarding Shabbat, we require something significant,
and this too — it is significant.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's second objection (step 4) and closes the exchange.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the reason for the measure
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The measure works by combining the wine with water that is not carried.
steps.terutzMaskana: Nothing is combined. The small amount of wine is significant by itself, and significance is what שבת requires.

steps.title: תוספתא: dried wine is measured by an olive-bulk
steps.stepSummary: A תוספתא teaches that dried-up (congealed) wine makes one liable when it is a כזית, according to רבי נתן.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: Dry wine is measured by a כזית — the words of רבי נתן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: what is the measure for wine that has dried up into a solid? This sets up רב יוסף's comparison in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once wine dries, it is no longer measured like a liquid. רבי נתן gives it the standard solid-food measure, a כזית.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught (in a ברייתא or תוספתא)
Olive-bulk, the standard measure for solids

phrases.english: It was taught: Dry (wine) — with an olive-bulk,
the words of Rabbi Natan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from liquid wine to dried wine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dried wine makes one liable at a כזית (רבי נתן).

steps.title: רב יוסף: רבי נתן and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה agree
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says that רבי נתן and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה hold the same idea. רבי נתן's view is the one just quoted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: רבי נתן and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה said the same thing. רבי נתן — what we just said.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף says two תנאים agree, and starts to show it. רבי נתן's half is the תוספתא we just saw. רבי יוסי's half comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The shared idea is that a liquid amount and a dried amount match up: a רביעית of liquid dries into a כזית. רב יוסף is setting up a comparison, and the proof for רבי יוסי follows in the next steps.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי נָתָן וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: Rabbi Natan and Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda
said one (the same) thing.
Rabbi Natan — that which we just said,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Links רבי נתן's ruling to another תנא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי נתן and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה share the same view on how liquid relates to a dried measure.

steps.title: ברייתא: בית שמאי and בית הלל on blood of a נבלה
steps.stepSummary: To show רבי יוסי's view, the גמרא quotes a ברייתא. רבי יהודה lists six cases where בית שמאי are lenient and בית הלל are strict. One of them: בית שמאי say the blood of a נבלה is טהור, and בית הלל say it is טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה — as it was taught: רבי יהודה says: Six things are among the leniencies of בית שמאי and the stringencies of בית הלל. Blood of a נבלה — בית שמאי declare it pure, and בית הלל declare it impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the background ברייתא needed for רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's statement, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually בית שמאי are the strict ones, so this list is unusual. Here בית הלל hold that the blood of a dead animal (נבלה) passes on impurity like its meat.

keyTerms.meaning: Blood of an animal that died without proper שחיטה

steps.confusionAlert: Normally בית שמאי are stricter. This ברייתא lists the rare cases where it is the other way around.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda — as it was taught:
Rabbi Yehuda says:
Six matters are among the leniencies of Beit Shammai
and among the stringencies of Beit Hillel.
Blood of a carcass —
Beit Shammai deem it pure,
and Beit Hillel deem it impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source for the second half of רב יוסף's comparison.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית הלל hold that the blood of a נבלה is טמא.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: a רביעית of blood congeals into an olive-bulk
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says בית הלל made blood impure only when there is a רביעית, because a רביעית can congeal into a כזית. This matches רבי נתן's idea that a dried liquid is measured by a כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה said: Even when בית הלל declared it impure, they declared impure only blood that has a רביעית, since it can congeal and stand at a כזית.
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes רב יוסף's proof. It shows that רבי יוסי also holds that a רביעית of liquid dries into a כזית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Meat of a נבלה is טמא at a כזית. Blood is treated as impure only at a רביעית, because when it dries it becomes a כזית. That is the same link between liquid and dried measures that רבי נתן used for wine.

keyTerms.meaning: To amount to, come out as

steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף's point: both רבי נתן and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה hold that a רביעית of liquid dries into a כזית. אביי challenges this comparison in the next two steps.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda said:
Even when Beit Hillel deemed it impure,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא טִמְּאוּ אֶלָּא בְּדָם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ רְבִיעִית,
phrases.english: they deemed impure only blood that contains a quarter-log,
since it can congeal
and amount to an olive-bulk.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוֹאִיל וְיָכוֹל לִקְרוֹשׁ וְלַעֲמוֹד עַל כְּזַיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי יוסי's statement on the ברייתא, which completes רב יוסף's comparison.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's claim that רבי נתן and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה agree
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's statement that a רביעית of blood congeals into a כזית

steps.title: אביי: רבי נתן may only be talking about thin wine
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the two views might not match. Maybe רבי נתן says a כזית needs a full רביעית only for wine, which is thin. Blood is thick, so a כזית of blood would not need a full רביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Maybe that is not so. רבי נתן only said here that a dried olive-bulk needs a quarter-log when he was talking about wine, which is thin. But for blood, which is thick, an olive-bulk does not need a full quarter-log.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי rejects רב יוסף's claim that the two תנאים hold the same view. He points out that wine and blood are different kinds of liquid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף's proof depended on treating wine and blood the same. אביי says thin wine shrinks a lot when it dries, so you need a full רביעית to get a כזית. Thick blood shrinks less, so less than a רביעית of blood is already a כזית, and the two rulings cannot be compared.

keyTerms.meaning: Maybe that is not so (a rejection formula)
He only said this in that specific case
A quarter of a לוג, a liquid measure

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not arguing about the הלכה itself. He is only saying that רב יוסף's comparison does not prove that the two תנאים agree.

phrases.english: Abaye said: Perhaps that is not so.

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי נָתָן הָכָא
phrases.english: Rabbi Natan only said here
that an olive-bulk requires a quarter-log
phrases.notes: That is, it takes a quarter-log of liquid to dry into an olive-bulk.

phrases.english: only with wine, which is thin
but with blood, which is thick
an olive-bulk does not require a quarter-log.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from step 11 that the two תנאים agree.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claimed match between רבי נתן and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof ignores the difference between thin wine and thick blood when they dry.

steps.title: אביי's second option: רבי יוסי may only be talking about thick blood
steps.stepSummary: אביי gives a second way to reject the comparison. Maybe רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says a רביעית makes a כזית only for thick blood. For thin wine, a כזית would come from more than a רביעית. Then, if we measured dried wine by its liquid size, someone carrying less than a כזית of dried wine should already be liable, which is not what רבי נתן says.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or else: רבי יוסי son of רבי יהודה only said there that a quarter-log is enough for an olive-bulk when talking about blood, which is thick. But wine is thin, so an olive-bulk of dried wine comes from more than a quarter-log. If so, even when someone carries out less than an olive-bulk, he should be liable.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי offers an alternative rejection. This time he limits רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's rule to blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a רביעית turns into a כזית only for thick blood, then a רביעית of thin wine dries into less than a כזית. If dried wine were measured by its liquid amount, carrying that smaller dried piece should already make him liable. רבי נתן requires a full כזית, so his rule is a separate measure and does not match רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: Carries out (from one domain to another on שבת)

steps.whatToRemember: Both of אביי's options rest on one point: thin wine and thick blood shrink differently when they dry. So רב יוסף's claim that רבי נתן and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה hold the same view is not proven.

phrases.english: Alternatively,

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה הָתָם
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda only said there
that a quarter-log is enough to make an olive-bulk
only with blood, which is thick
but wine, which is thin,
an olive-bulk comes from more than a quarter-log
so even when he carries out less than an olive-bulk, let him be liable.
phrases.notes: This shows that רבי נתן, who requires a full olive-bulk, cannot hold the same idea as רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נָמֵי, עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, alternative way to reject the comparison rejected in step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claimed match between the two תנאים
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: If רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's rule applies only to blood, then measuring dried wine by its liquid amount would make one liable for less than a כזית. That contradicts רבי נתן.

steps.title: Is the משנה's word for 'gulp' spelled with an א or an ע?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's phrase 'milk: כדי גמיעה' and asks how the word is spelled: with an א or with an ע.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: milk, the amount of a gulp. They asked: Is it 'גמיאה' with an א, or 'גמיעה' with an ע?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה, about how much milk one must carry to be liable. It asks a spelling question about the key word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two spellings sound almost the same, but the גמרא wants the correct גירסא (wording) of the משנה. This is a question about wording, not about the amount itself.

keyTerms.meaning: The amount of one gulp or swallow
They asked; a question was raised before the חכמים

phrases.english: [The Mishnah taught:] Milk, the amount of a gulp.
They asked:
Is it 'gemi'ah' with an aleph, or 'gemi'ah' with an ayin?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the wine and blood discussion and moves to the next line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The correct spelling of the משנה's word for 'gulp': with an א or with an ע.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק proves the spelling with an א from a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that the word is spelled with an א. He brings the פסוק about אליעזר and רבקה, 'הגמיאיני נא מעט מים מכדך', which uses an א.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: It is with an א, as the פסוק says, 'Please let me swallow a little water from your jug.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers the spelling question with a פסוק that uses the same root, spelled with an א.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה uses the word for swallowing with an א when אליעזר asks רבקה for water. So the משנה's word should be spelled the same way, 'גמיאה'.

keyTerms.meaning: Let me swallow (spelled with an א)

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
